mainTopic: A repentant כהן who served עבודה זרה (רב נחמן vs. רב ששת), and the story of בית חוניו
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a מחלוקת between רב נחמן and רב ששת. The question is whether a כהן who served עבודה זרה and then did תשובה may serve again in the בית המקדש. רב נחמן proves from a ברייתא that a כהן who slaughtered for an idol on purpose and repented may serve. רב ששת answers that the ברייתא is talking about an accidental case. The גמרא then shows that they argue the same way about bowing to an idol and about declaring it a god, and explains why each of the four cases had to be taught. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה and infers from its wording that בית חוניו was not עבודה זרה. A ברייתא tells the story of שמעון הצדיק's death and the jealousy between his sons חוניו and שמעי. In רבי מאיר's version, חוניו built an idolatrous altar in Egypt. In רבי יהודה's version, he built it לשם שמים, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו. Along the way, the חכמים, רבי יהושע בן פרחיה and the story of שאול teach how people cling to power. At the end, אביי explains how רבי מאיר reads רבי יהודה's פסוק: it is about princes whom חזקיה made vow to give up עבודה זרה, and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ששת's reason: he became an idolatrous priest
steps.stepSummary: The end of רב ששת's reason: a כהן who slaughtered for עבודה זרה is disqualified because he has become a כומר for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He became a priest for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the sugya in the middle. This line finishes רב ששת's reason for saying the כהן is disqualified from serving in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By slaughtering for an idol on purpose, the כהן acted as the idol's priest. In רב ששת's view, that alone ruins his status for the בית המקדש, even though it was 'only' שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest who serves an idol
Idol worship

phrases.english: He became a priest for idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב ששת's position from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who slaughtered for עבודה זרה is disqualified, because he became a כומר for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא about a כהן who repented
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a ברייתא: a כהן who served עבודה זרה and then repented, his קרבן is still a pleasing aroma.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Where do I get my view from? From a ברייתא: a כהן who served idols and then repented, his offering is a pleasing aroma.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a source to support his view that the כהן can still serve. This step sets up the source, and the next step explains exactly how it proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says plainly that repentance brings the כהן back, so his קרבן is accepted. On its face, that goes against רב ששת, who says the כהן stays disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof)
And he repented (did תשובה)
A pleasing aroma, meaning the קרבן is accepted

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: From where do I say it?
As it is taught: A priest who served idol worship,
and repented, his offering is a pleasing aroma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת by bringing a ברייתא that seems to support רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that a כהן who slaughtered for עבודה זרה and repented may serve.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a כהן who served עבודה זרה and repented, his קרבן is a pleasing aroma.

steps.title: Narrowing the ברייתא down to intentional slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן shows the ברייתא cannot mean an accidental case, and cannot mean זריקה, so it must mean intentional שחיטה. That is exactly his case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is it talking about? If it was accidental, why say 'and repented'? He was never really a sinner! So it must be on purpose. And if he did sprinkling of the blood, what good does repenting do? He already performed real service for the idol! So it must be talking about slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן works out which case the ברייתא must mean by ruling out the other options. He ends up with a כהן who slaughtered for an idol on purpose and then repented, and that כהן is allowed to serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, 'repented' only makes sense if he sinned on purpose (מזיד). Second, זריקה is real service, so a כהן who did it for an idol stays disqualified even after repenting. The only case left is intentional שחיטה, and there the ברייתא says repentance works, which goes against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (tries out one possible reading)
Unintentional, by mistake
Intentional, on purpose
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, a core priestly service
Service, real priestly ministry
Slaughtering the animal

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא is about an accidental case. רב נחמן's whole proof rests on showing it must be intentional, because 'he repented' only fits someone who sinned on purpose.

phrases.english: In what case?
If we say it was unwitting,
what is 'and repented'? He already stands repentant!
phrases.notes: Someone who sinned by accident never meant to sin, so there is nothing to repent from.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously intentional.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בִּזְרִיקָה – כִּי שָׁב מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: And if it was sprinkling, when he repents, what of it?
He has performed service for it!
Rather, is it not about slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא from step 2 proves רב נחמן's view, by ruling out the other possible cases.
steps.raayaObject: That intentional שחיטה for עבודה זרה does not permanently disqualify a כהן who repents.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא read by elimination: not שוגג (no need to repent), not זריקה (real service), so it must be intentional שחיטה.

steps.title: רב ששת reads the ברייתא as an accidental case
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the ברייתא is about an accidental case. 'Repented' means he was never really guilty to begin with. If he acted on purpose, his קרבן is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת can say: really it is about an accidental case. This is what the ברייתא means: if he was 'repentant' from the start, because he did it by mistake, his offering is a pleasing aroma. If not, his offering is not a pleasing aroma.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב ששת would push back on רב נחמן's proof. He reads 'and repented' differently, so the ברייתא no longer supports רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן assumed 'repented' must mean someone who sinned on purpose. רב ששת reads it as 'he was never really a sinner,' meaning he acted by mistake. So the ברייתא is really drawing a line: שוגג is accepted, מזיד is not, and that fits רב ששת exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (keeps a reading that was rejected)
And this is what it means (rereads the source)
Repentant from the start, never truly guilty

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: the ברייתא is about intentional שחיטה, so a כהן who repents may serve. רב ששת: the ברייתא only accepts the accidental case. If he slaughtered on purpose, his קרבן is not accepted, because he became a כומר for עבודה זרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא: one side reads a word in a ברייתא (here 'repented') in an unexpected way, and the proof against him falls apart.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet could say to you:
Actually, it is about an unwitting case,
and this is what it is saying:
If he was repentant from the outset,
since when he served, he served unwittingly,
his offering is a pleasing aroma;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – אֵין קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ.
phrases.english: and if not, his offering is not a pleasing aroma.
phrases.notes: 'If not' means he did it on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר לָךְ, לְעוֹלָם בְּשׁוֹגֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב נחמן's proof by bringing back the שוגג reading he had ruled out.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב נחמן's proof from the ברייתא. It does not prove רב ששת's view, it only takes away the support for רב נחמן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן assumed 'and repented' must mean a deliberate sinner. It can also mean 'he was never truly guilty,' meaning he acted by mistake.

steps.title: Two more disputes: bowing and declaring
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב ששת also argue about a כהן who bowed to עבודה זרה and a כהן who acknowledged it as a god. רב נחמן says his later קרבן is a רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ, and רב ששת says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a כהן bowed to an idol, רב נחמן says his offering is a pleasing aroma, and רב ששת says it is not. If he declared the idol a god, רב נחמן says his offering is a pleasing aroma, and רב ששת says it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists two more cases where the same two אמוראים argue in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we saw their dispute about a כהן who did זריקה or שחיטה for עבודה זרה. Now the same dispute is applied to bowing (an action, but not a sacrificial service) and to acknowledging (only words). The positions stay the same: רב נחמן is lenient, רב ששת is strict.

keyTerms.meaning: He bowed down (to an idol)
He acknowledged / declared (the idol to be a god)
A pleasing aroma, meaning the קרבן is accepted by ה׳
His offering (the קרבן he brings later in the בית המקדש)

phrases.english: If he bowed to an idol:
phrases.notes: 'He' is a כהן who later repented and came back to serve in the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman says: his offering is a pleasing aroma,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֵין קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ.
phrases.english: and Rav Sheshet says: his offering is not a pleasing aroma.
If he acknowledged an idol as a god:

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman says: his offering is a pleasing aroma,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֵין קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ.
phrases.english: and Rav Sheshet says: his offering is not a pleasing aroma.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the debate over the שחיטה case, the גמרא lists two parallel disputes between the same אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For bowing and for acknowledging עבודה זרה, רב נחמן accepts the כהן's later קרבן and רב ששת does not.

steps.title: Why the slaughter case was needed after the sprinkling case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why all the disputes are needed. From the first case (זריקה) alone, we might think רב ששת is strict only because זריקה is a real Temple service, and that he would agree with רב נחמן about שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the cases are needed. If we had been taught only the first case, we would say that רב ששת is strict there because the כהן did a real Temple-type service for the idol. But in slaughter, which is not that kind of service, I would say he agrees with רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks, without saying it out loud, why we need four separate disputes, and starts answering with the first two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זריקה is a service only a כהן may do, so it is called שֵׁירוּת. שחיטה is less than that. So without the שחיטה dispute, we could have thought רב ששת is lenient there. Teaching the שחיטה case shows he is strict even then.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, meaning each case teaches something the others could not
Service, here a real Temple-style service like זריקה
Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן, a central Temple service
I would have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the גמרא calls שחיטה the weaker case, and in the next step it calls שחיטה the stronger case. There is no contradiction. It is a ladder: שחיטה is less than זריקה, but more than bowing.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if it had taught us only that first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is the earlier dispute about a כהן who did זריקה for an idol by mistake.

phrases.english: in that case Rav Sheshet says [he is disqualified]
because he performed a real service for it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁחִיטָה דְּלָא עֲבַד לֵיהּ שֵׁירוּת –
phrases.english: but slaughter, where he did not perform a real service for it,
I would say he agrees with Rav Nachman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing all four disputes, the גמרא explains why each one is needed, starting with זריקה and שחיטה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why were all four disputes needed, if the same two positions apply in each?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The זריקה case alone would suggest רב ששת is strict only for a real service like זריקה. The שחיטה case teaches he is strict even without that.

steps.title: Why the bowing case was needed after the slaughter case
steps.stepSummary: From the שחיטה case alone, we might think רב ששת is strict because the כהן did a real act of worship. Bowing is not that kind of act, so we might think he is lenient there. So the bowing case is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had been taught only slaughter, we would say he is strict because he did an act of worship for the idol. But bowing, where he did not do an act of worship, I would say no. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves one step down the ladder: from slaughter to bowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה is still a sacrificial act (עֲבוֹדָה). Bowing has no קרבן at all. Without this dispute, we might limit רב ששת's strictness to sacrificial acts. The bowing case shows he is strict even for bowing.

keyTerms.meaning: An act of worship that is part of bringing a קרבן
Slaughtering the animal

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only slaughter,
[I would say he is disqualified] because he performed an act of worship for it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה דְּלָא עֲבַד לֵיהּ עֲבוֹדָה –
phrases.english: but if he bowed, where he did not perform an act of worship for it,
I would say not. So it is necessary.
phrases.notes: 'Not' means רב ששת would not disqualify him. That is why the bowing case had to be taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכא ladder, from שחיטה down to bowing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the bowing dispute needed if we already know the שחיטה dispute?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שחיטה is a sacrificial act and bowing is not, so we might think רב ששת is lenient for bowing. Teaching it shows he is not.

steps.title: Why the declaring case was needed after the bowing case
steps.stepSummary: From the bowing case alone, we might think רב ששת is strict because bowing is a physical action. Declaring the idol a god is only words, so we might think he is lenient there. So this case is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had been taught only bowing, we would say he is strict because he did an action for the idol. But declaring, which is only speech, I would say no. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ladder with the lowest case: just saying the idol is a god.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bowing is still an action of the body. Declaring is only words. By teaching this case too, the גמרא shows that רב ששת disqualifies the כהן even when he did nothing more than speak.

keyTerms.meaning: A physical action
Mere speech, only words

steps.whatToRemember: Four levels, from strongest to weakest: זריקה (real Temple service), שחיטה (a sacrificial act), bowing (a physical action), declaring (only words). רב ששת disqualifies the repentant כהן's later קרבן at every level. רב נחמן accepts it at every level.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how strict רב ששת's view really is: any act of עבודה זרה, even just words, makes the כהן's later קרבן not a רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only bowing,
[I would say he is disqualified] because he performed an action for it,
but if he acknowledged it, which is mere speech,
I would say not. So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא ladder, from bowing down to mere speech.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All four disputes are needed, because each case is weaker than the one before. רב ששת is strict even for mere words.

steps.title: The משנה's wording shows בית חוניו is not idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that, needless to say, כהנים who served עבודה זרה are disqualified. The גמרא infers that the משנה treats בית חוניו as something different from עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And needless to say, something else' (idol worship). Because it says 'needless to say' about idol worship, we learn that the temple of חוניו is not idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next line. From the way that line is worded, it draws a conclusion about בית חוניו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'needless to say' means idol worship is an even worse case than the one the משנה just discussed. So the משנה must see כהנים who served in בית חוניו as less bad than idol worshippers. That means בית חוניו was a temple built to serve ה׳, even though it was outside ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Something else.' A polite way of saying עבודה זרה, idol worship.
'Needless to say.' It shows that the next case is even more obvious than the case before it.
'By inference.' We learn this from what the words imply.
The temple built by חוניו in Egypt, outside ירושלים.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית חוניו is being called kosher. The משנה still says its כהנים are disqualified from serving in the בית המקדש. The only point here is that it is not as bad as idol worship.

phrases.english: And needless to say, something else, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Something else' is a polite way of saying idol worship.

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּקָאָמַר: אֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דָּבָר אַחֵר,
phrases.english: From the fact that it says: needless to say, something else,
we can infer that the temple of Onias
is not idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר: אֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דָּבָר אַחֵר, מִכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion of the רב נחמן / רב ששת disputes is finished. The גמרא returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the wording of the משנה, בית חוניו is not עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this view: the year שמעון הצדיק died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא supporting the view that בית חוניו is not עבודה זרה. It begins with שמעון הצדיק predicting his own death.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports the one who says בית חוניו is not idol worship. In the year שמעון הצדיק died, he told people, 'This year he will die.' They asked him, 'How do you know?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא as support and starts telling its story. The connection to בית חוניו will only become clear later in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'like the one who says' tell us there is a disagreement about בית חוניו. This ברייתא records both רבי מאיר's and רבי יהודה's versions, and the support comes from רבי יהודה's version (see step 20). The story opens by setting the scene with שמעון הצדיק's prediction and the people's question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the one who says.' This source supports one side of a disagreement.
'From where do you know?' A request for the source of what someone knows.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא like the one who says

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית חוֹנְיוֹ לָאו עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא,
phrases.english: the temple of Onias is not idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה שֶׁמֵּת שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק,
phrases.english: as it is taught: That year in which Shimon HaTzaddik died,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: שָׁנָה זוֹ הוּא מֵת,
phrases.english: he said to them: This year he will die,
phrases.notes: He is talking about himself. He says 'he' instead of 'I' so he does not speak of his own death directly.

phrases.english: They said to him: From where do you know?

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר בֵּית חוֹנְיוֹ לָאו עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for the inference made in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The view that בית חוניו is not עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the death of שמעון הצדיק, which continues past this point.

steps.title: The old man in white and the old man in black
steps.stepSummary: שמעון הצדיק explains his vision. Every year an old man dressed in white went in and out with him on יום הכפורים. This year the old man was dressed in black and did not come out with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Every יום הכפורים an old man dressed and wrapped in white would meet me. He went in with me and came out with me. This year an old man dressed and wrapped in black met me. He went in with me but did not come out with me.
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון הצדיק answers the question 'How do you know?' by describing a vision he had in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two contrasts: white has changed to black, and coming out with him has changed to not coming out. Both are signs of death. שמעון הצדיק understood the vision as telling him he would die that year.

keyTerms.meaning: The day the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל enters the קודש הקדשים.
'One old man,' the figure in the vision.
'Wrapped,' as in a head covering or cloak.
'White' and 'black' clothing.

phrases.english: He said to them: Every Yom Kippur

phrases.aramaic: נִזְדַּמֵּן לִי זָקֵן אֶחָד לָבוּשׁ לְבָנִים,
phrases.english: an old man dressed in white would meet me,
and wrapped in white,
and he would go in with me and come out with me.
phrases.notes: He means going into the קודש הקדשים, where the כהן גדול is supposed to go in alone.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁנָה זוֹ נִזְדַּמֵּן לִי זָקֵן אֶחָד לָבוּשׁ שְׁחוֹרִים,
phrases.english: This year an old man dressed in black met me,
and wrapped in black,
and he went in with me but did not come out with me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: כׇּל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים נִזְדַּמֵּן לִי זָקֵן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 10, 'From where do you know?'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How שמעון הצדיק knew he would die that year.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His yearly vision changed: the old man was in black and did not come out with him.

steps.title: שמעון הצדיק dies, and the כהנים stop blessing with the Name
steps.stepSummary: After סוכות, שמעון הצדיק was sick for seven days and died. After his death the כהנים stopped saying ברכת כהנים with the special Name of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the festival he was sick for seven days and died. His fellow כהנים then stopped blessing with the Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the prediction comes true, and the ברייתא describes a change that followed his death. The story goes on past this point and will connect to בית חוניו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death after סוכות shows that the vision was true. The fact that the כהנים stopped using the special Name shows how much was lost when שמעון הצדיק died. This sets the scene for the next part of the story about who would take his place.

keyTerms.meaning: A pilgrimage festival. Here it means סוכות, which comes right after יום הכפורים.
To say ברכת כהנים using the special Name of ה׳.
'His brothers the כהנים,' meaning his fellow כהנים.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's wording shows that בית חוניו is not עבודה זרה, and a ברייתא about the death of שמעון הצדיק is brought to support this. The story continues beyond this point.

phrases.english: After the festival,
phrases.notes: This is סוכות, which comes right after יום כיפור.

phrases.english: he was sick for seven days and died,
and his fellow priests refrained
from blessing with the Name.
phrases.notes: He means ברכת כהנים said with ה׳'s special Name.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַחַר הָרֶגֶל, חָלָה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the vision in step 11 coming true and continues the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמעון הצדיק died after סוכות, and the כהנים stopped blessing with the special Name.

steps.title: שמעון הצדיק names חוניו, and שמעי becomes jealous
steps.stepSummary: As he is dying, שמעון הצדיק names his son חוניו as the next כהן גדול. חוניו's older brother שמעי becomes jealous.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he was dying, he told them: My son חוניו will serve in my place. His brother שמעי, who was two and a half years older, became jealous of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story of שמעון הצדיק. This opens רבי מאיר's version of how בית חוניו began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new כהן גדול is the younger son, חוניו. Because שמעי is older, he feels passed over. That jealousy drives everything that happens next in רבי מאיר's version.

keyTerms.meaning: Passing away, death
Will serve in my place (as כהן גדול)
Became jealous

phrases.english: At the time of his passing, he said to them:
Chonyo my son will serve in my place.
Shimi his brother became jealous of him,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה.
phrases.english: for he was older than him by two and a half years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא right after the death of שמעון הצדיק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוניו is appointed כהן גדול, and his older brother שמעי becomes jealous.

steps.title: שמעי tricks חוניו into looking disgraceful
steps.stepSummary: שמעי offers to teach חוניו the service. He dresses him in a woman's tunic and belt and tells the כהנים that חוניו is keeping a promise to his lover.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעי said: Come, I'll teach you the order of the service. He dressed him in a tunic and tied a ribbon on him as a belt, and stood him next to the מזבח. Then he told the other כהנים: Look what this man promised his beloved and kept: 'On the day I serve as כהן גדול, I will wear your tunic and tie on your belt.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמעי pretends to help his brother. In fact he sets him up to look like he is disgracing the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the כהן גדול's special garments, חוניו is dressed in a woman's clothing. שמעי then invents a story that this was a promise to a woman. The other כהנים will now see חוניו as mocking the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the Temple service
A tunic (here, a woman's garment)
A ribbon or sash worn as a belt
The position of כהן גדול
His beloved (a woman)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בֹּא וַאֲלַמֶּדְךָ סֵדֶר עֲבוֹדָה.
phrases.english: He said to him: Come and I will teach you the order of the service.
He dressed him in a tunic and belted him with a ribbon,
and stood him next to the altar.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, just adds "and".

phrases.english: He said to his fellow priests:

phrases.aramaic: רְאוּ מָה נָדַר זֶה וְקִיֵּים לַאֲהוּבָתוֹ:
phrases.english: See what this one vowed and fulfilled for his beloved:
"On the day that I serve as High Priest

phrases.aramaic: אֶלְבּוֹשׁ בְּאוּנְקְלִי שֶׁלִּיכִי וְאֶחְגּוֹר בְּצִילְצוֹל שֶׁלִּיכִי״.
phrases.english: I will wear your tunic and tie on your ribbon."
phrases.notes: שליכי means "yours," said to a woman. So these are her clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בֹּא וַאֲלַמֶּדְךָ סֵדֶר עֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how שמעי acted on the jealousy from step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמעי publicly humiliates חוניו with a made-up story about a promise to a woman.

steps.title: חוניו runs away and builds an altar for עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים want to kill חוניו. He runs away to Alexandria in Egypt, builds a מזבח there, and offers on it for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: His fellow כהנים wanted to kill him. He ran from them, and they chased him. He went to Alexandria in Egypt, built a מזבח there, and brought offerings on it for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: According to רבי מאיר, the humiliated חוניו runs away and starts an idolatrous altar in Egypt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, בית חוניו is a place of עבודה זרה. That is the key detail the two versions will argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: To kill him
Alexandria in Egypt
Idol worship

phrases.english: His fellow priests wanted to kill him,
he ran from them, and they ran after him.
He went to Alexandria in Egypt,
and built an altar there,
and offered upon it for the sake of idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of the humiliation in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי מאיר's version, בית חוניו was built for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The חכמים learn a lesson about jealousy over a position
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say: if someone who never even held the position acted this way, then someone who did hold it would act even worse. This closes רבי מאיר's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים heard about it, they said: If this one, who never took the position, acted like this, then someone who did take it would surely act worse. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים draw a moral from the story. This marks the end of רבי מאיר's account.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning compares a smaller case to a bigger one. Someone who never held the post still caused this much harm out of jealousy. So someone who held it and lost it would be even more dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down into it, meaning took up the position
All the more so

phrases.english: And when the Sages heard of the matter, they said:

phrases.aramaic: מָה זֶה שֶׁלֹּא יָרַד לָהּ – כָּךְ,
phrases.english: If this one, who did not enter into it, acted like this,
phrases.notes: "Entering into it" means taking on the job of כהן גדול.

phrases.aramaic: הַיּוֹרֵד לָהּ – עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: then one who does enter into it, all the more so.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי מאיר's version with the חכמים's lesson
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר's version ends with בית חוניו as עבודה זרה and a warning about jealousy over positions.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the story happened differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects רבי מאיר's version. חוניו actually turned down the job because שמעי was older, but later became jealous of שמעי anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: That is not how it happened. Rather, חוניו did not accept the position, because his brother שמעי was two and a half years older. Even so, חוניו became jealous of his brother שמעי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר and starts telling his own version of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roles are switched. Here חוניו gives the job to the older שמעי, and חוניו is the jealous one. So חוניו is the trickster, not the victim.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not how the event happened
Did not accept upon himself (the position)
And even so

steps.confusionAlert: Watch who is who. In רבי מאיר's version שמעי tricks חוניו. In רבי יהודה's version חוניו tricks שמעי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him: The incident was not like this,
rather, Chonyo did not accept it upon himself,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה שִׁמְעִי אָחִיו גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה,
phrases.english: because Shimi his brother was older than him by two and a half years,
and even so,
Chonyo became jealous of Shimi his brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's account and starts a different one
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole of רבי מאיר's account of who was jealous and who was humiliated
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר switched the roles. חוניו gave up the job and was the jealous one.

steps.title: חוניו tricks שמעי the same way
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's version, חוניו plays the same trick on שמעי: the woman's clothes and the made-up promise to a lover.
steps.simpleTranslation: חוניו said to שמעי: Come, I'll teach you the order of the service. He dressed him in a tunic, tied a ribbon on him as a belt, and stood him next to the מזבח. Then he told the other כהנים: Look what this man promised his beloved and kept: 'On the day he serves as כהן גדול, I will wear your tunic and tie on your belt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same trick from step 14 is told again, but now חוניו does it to שמעי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are almost exactly the same as before, so the story is identical except for who plays which role. That makes חוניו the guilty one before he ever reaches Egypt.

keyTerms.meaning: He dressed him
And he belted him
Vowed and fulfilled

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בֹּא וַאֲלַמֶּדְךָ סֵדֶר עֲבוֹדָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: Come and I will teach you the order of the service,
and he dressed him in a tunic and belted him with a ribbon,
and stood him next to the altar.
He said to his fellow priests:

phrases.aramaic: רְאוּ מָה נָדַר זֶה וְקִיֵּים לַאֲהוּבָתוֹ
phrases.english: See what this one vowed and fulfilled for his beloved:
"On the day that he serves as High Priest

phrases.aramaic: אֶלְבּוֹשׁ בְּאוּנְקְלִי שֶׁלִּיכִי וְאֶחְגּוֹר בְּצִילְצוֹל שֶׁלִּיכִי״.
phrases.english: I will wear your tunic and tie on your ribbon."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בֹּא וַאֲלַמֶּדְךָ סֵדֶר עֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's version with the trick, now done by חוניו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוניו humiliates שמעי with the made-up story about a promise to a woman.

steps.title: The plot is exposed and חוניו runs away
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים want to kill שמעי, but he tells them the whole story. They turn on חוניו, who runs, even to the king's palace, and is recognized everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: His fellow כהנים wanted to kill him. He told them everything that had happened, so they wanted to kill חוניו. חוניו ran from them, and they chased him. He ran to the king's palace, and they chased him there too. Everyone who saw him said: That's him, that's him!
steps.whatsHappening: שמעי clears his name, and now חוניו is the one being hunted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי מאיר's version, the victim explains what really happened. חוניו cannot hide anywhere, which sets up why he leaves the country entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: Told, related
What happened, the incident
The king's palace

phrases.english: His fellow priests wanted to kill him,
phrases.notes: "Him" here is שמעי, the one dressed up in this version.

phrases.english: he told them the whole incident,
so they wanted to kill Chonyo,
he ran from them, and they ran after him,
he ran to the king's palace, and they ran after him,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָרוֹאֶה אוֹתוֹ אוֹמֵר: זֶה הוּא, זֶה הוּא,
phrases.english: everyone who saw him would say: This is him, this is him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Result of the trick in רבי יהודה's version
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוניו's trick is exposed and he is chased with nowhere to hide.

steps.title: חוניו builds an altar in Egypt לשם שמים, backed by a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: חוניו goes to Alexandria and builds a מזבח for the sake of Heaven. רבי יהודה supports this with a פסוק in ישעיהו about an altar to ה׳ in Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to Alexandria in Egypt, built a מזבח there, and brought offerings on it לשם שמים. As the פסוק says: 'On that day there will be an altar to ה׳ in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to ה׳ at its border.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה ends his version: בית חוניו was built to serve ה׳, not idols, and he brings a פסוק to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the main point of the dispute. For רבי מאיר, בית חוניו was עבודה זרה. For רבי יהודה it was a מזבח to ה׳, but built in Egypt, far from the בית המקדש in ירושלים. This matches the גמרא's inference in step 9 that the משנה treats בית חוניו differently from עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of Heaven, to serve ה׳
A pillar or monument
Its border

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: בית חוניו was עבודה זרה. רבי יהודה: it was לשם שמים, as in the פסוק in ישעיהו. The משנה, which treats בית חוניו as different from עבודה זרה, fits רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether בית חוניו was idolatry or a misplaced service to ה׳ decides how its כהנים are treated in the משנה.

phrases.english: He went to Alexandria in Egypt,
and built an altar there,
and offered upon it for the sake of Heaven,
as it is stated: "On that day
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 19:19. The word in round brackets is not in the פסוק itself, so the corrected text leaves it out.

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיֶה מִזְבֵּחַ לַה׳ בְּתוֹךְ אֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם
phrases.english: there will be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt,
and a pillar at its border to the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends רבי יהודה's version, in contrast to step 15
steps.raayaObject: That בית חוניו was built לשם שמים and is different from עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 19:19, which speaks of an altar to ה׳ in Egypt

steps.title: The חכמים's lesson in רבי יהודה's version
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say: חוניו ran away from the job of כהן גדול and still became this jealous. Someone who actually wants a position will surely be even more jealous.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים heard about it, they said: If this man, who ran away from the position, acted like this, then someone who wants to get the position will act even worse.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים draw a lesson from רבי יהודה's version of the story, and this closes that version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's telling, חוניו himself turned down the job of כהן גדול, yet he still tried to get שמעי killed out of jealousy. The חכמים reason with a קל וחומר: if someone who never wanted the job got this jealous, someone who does want it will be far more jealous. This parallels the lesson in Step 16 from רבי מאיר's version, but now it is built on רבי יהודה's facts.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; the wording of a קל וחומר
Ran away from it, meaning he turned down the position
Literally 'to go down into it,' meaning to take the position

steps.confusionAlert: This looks a lot like Step 16, but it is not a repeat. Step 16 was the lesson in רבי מאיר's version. This is the matching lesson in רבי יהודה's version, where חוניו turned the job down himself.

phrases.english: And when the Sages heard of the matter,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: וּמָה זֶה שֶׁבָּרַח מִמֶּנָּה כָּךְ,
phrases.english: they said: If this one, who fled from it, [acted] like this,
phrases.notes: "It" is the job of כהן גדול, which חוניו turned down in רבי יהודה's version.

phrases.english: one who wants to enter into it
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי יהודה's version of the story with the lesson the חכמים take from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Jealousy over positions of honor is so strong that even someone who turned the job down can be overcome by it. Someone who wants the job will feel it even more.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן פרחיה: how power changes a person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן פרחיה says that at first he would have punished anyone who urged him to take the leadership. Now that he has it, he would scald anyone who told him to leave it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי יהושע בן פרחיה said: At first, if anyone told me 'Take the position,' I would tie him up and throw him before a lion. Now, if anyone tells me to step down from it, I would throw a kettle of boiling water on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that fits the lesson of the חכמים. A great leader admits how his own feelings about power flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before he took the job, רבי יהושע בן פרחיה did not want it at all. Once he held it, he could not bear the thought of losing it. This supports the point of the חכמים: holding a position creates a strong attachment and jealousy.

keyTerms.meaning: Go up to it, meaning take the leadership position
I would tie him up
Lion
A kettle of hot (boiling) water

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָה:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya said:
At first, anyone who would say "Go up to it"
phrases.notes: "It" means the leadership position he later held.

phrases.english: I would tie him up and put him in front of a lion;

phrases.aramaic: עַתָּה, כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר לִי לֵירֵד מִמֶּנָּה –
phrases.english: now, anyone who tells me to step down from it

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי מֵטִיל עָלָיו קוּמְקוּם שֶׁל חַמִּין.
phrases.english: I would throw a kettle of boiling water on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching that backs up the lesson of the חכמים about how people cling to power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who did not want a position at first can become fiercely attached to it once he holds it.

steps.title: Proof from שאול המלך
steps.stepSummary: שאול ran away from becoming king. Once he was king, he tried to kill דוד to keep the throne.
steps.simpleTranslation: For שאול ran away from the kingship, and once he became king, he tried to kill דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its point from the story of שאול in תנ״ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול at first hid so he would not be made king. After he was king, he chased דוד to kill him. This shows the same flip that רבי יהושע בן פרחיה described: first a person runs from power, then he fights to keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: For behold; introduces a proof
Sought to kill

steps.whatToRemember: The main lesson of this whole story: people who once ran from honor can become dangerously jealous once they have it. We see it in חוניו, in רבי יהושע בן פרחיה's own words, and in שאול.

phrases.english: For Shaul fled from it,
phrases.notes: He hid among the baggage so he would not be made king (שמואל א 10:22).

phrases.english: and when he went up to it, he tried to kill David.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a proof from a פסוק-based story for the teaching in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a person who ran from power will fight to keep it once he has it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of שאול, who hid from becoming king and later tried to kill דוד.

steps.title: How does רבי מאיר explain רבי יהודה's verse?
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא asks אביי: רבי יהודה used a פסוק in ישעיהו about an altar to ה׳ in Egypt. How does רבי מאיר, who disagrees, explain that פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא, son of רב חסדא, said to אביי: What does רבי מאיר do with this verse that רבי יהודה used?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and goes back to the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. It is setting up the next move, an explanation of how רבי מאיר reads the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, רבי יהודה used the פסוק 'there will be an altar to ה׳ in the land of Egypt' to show that חוניו's מזבח was for the sake of Heaven. In רבי מאיר's version, חוניו's temple was for עבודה זרה. So the question is how רבי מאיר reads that פסוק, since he cannot be ignoring it.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse (פסוק)
What does he do with it? How does he explain it?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Chisda, said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir, this verse of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק רבי יהודה quoted in Step 20 (ישעיהו 19:19).

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side lesson about jealousy and returns to the disagreement over the פסוק from Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי מאיר explains the פסוק in ישעיהו about an altar to ה׳ in Egypt, given his view that חוניו's temple was for עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's version of the story
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק seems to speak well of an altar to ה׳ in Egypt, which seems to fit רבי יהודה's version better than רבי מאיר's.

steps.title: רבי מאיר reads the פסוק as being about חזקיה and the princes
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי מאיר uses the פסוק for a ברייתא: after סנחריב fell, חזקיה made the captive princes vow not to serve עבודה זרה, and the פסוק in ישעיהו is about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר uses that פסוק for what a ברייתא teaches. After סנחריב fell, חזקיה went out and found princes sitting in golden carriages. He made them vow not to serve idols, as the פסוק says: 'On that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer to מר קשישא's question from Step 24. רבי מאיר says the פסוק in ישעיהו is not about חוניו's מזבח. It is about foreign princes who promised חזקיה to stop serving idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the פסוק to show that חוניו's altar was built for the sake of Heaven. רבי מאיר takes away that proof by connecting the prophecy to a different event: the princes whom חזקיה made vow to give up עבודה זרה. So the altar to ה׳ in Egypt that the prophecy describes need not be חוניו's. The rest of this ברייתא continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: his downfall (here, the defeat of סנחריב's army)
princes, sons of kings
carriages or wagons
he made them take a vow (נדר)
idol worship
the language of Canaan, meaning לשון הקודש (Hebrew)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר agrees that the פסוק supports חוניו. His whole point is that the פסוק is about something else, so it gives no proof for חוניו's altar.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects רבי מאיר's view of חוניו. Without it, רבי יהודה's פסוק would seem to be a strong proof against him.

phrases.english: For that which is taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: This is אביי's answer: רבי מאיר uses the פסוק for the teaching that follows.

phrases.english: After the downfall of Sennacherib,
Hezekiah went out and found
princes who were sitting
in carriages of gold.
He made them vow not to worship idols,
as it is stated:
"In that day there shall be five cities
in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 19:18. This is part of the same prophecy רבי יהודה quoted about the altar in Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24 by showing how רבי מאיר explains the פסוק that רבי יהודה used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר reads the ישעיהו prophecy as being about the foreign princes whom חזקיה made vow to give up עבודה זרה. It is not about an altar built by חוניו.
